title: Adoptive cell transfer of macrophages following peripheral nerve injury in mice
protocol: Euthanize the mouse using CO2 asphyxiation followed by cervical dislocation.
Spray the euthanized mouse with 70% EtOH before dissection.
Dissect the whole leg, from hip to ankle, and soak it in 70% EtOH for 5 minutes in a 10-cm Petri dish.
Remove skin and skeletal muscle tissue from bones using forceps and scissors.
Wash the bone with cold PBS to avoid compromising sterility of bone marrow.
Separate the femur and tibia by cutting at the knee joint.
Clean away any remaining tissue and wash again with PBS in a new dish.
Extract bone marrow from the femur and tibia.
Fill a 1-mL syringe with cold bone marrow isolation buffer (BMIB).
Make fresh BMIB by adding 1.5 mL FBS to 48.5 mL PBS (3% final concentration of FBS).
Keep the BMIB on ice before use.
Cut off the ends of the femur bone and gently insert a 27-gauge needle attached to the syringe into the marrow cavity.
Flush the bone marrow into a 6-well plate or 10-cm Petri dish by expelling the BMIB through the cavity.
Refill the syringe with BMIB and repeat flushing until all the bone marrow material is in the plate or dish.
Repeat the process for tibia bones or additional animal bones.
Maintain sterility throughout the procedure.
Perform the entire procedure in a laminar flow hood.
Sterilize surgical equipment periodically with generous amounts of 70% EtOH.
Gently pipette the bone marrow mixture up and down to homogenize it.
Transfer the solution into a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C to pellet cells.
Aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL Red Blood Cell Lysis Buffer.
Incubate for 3–5 min at room temperature to lyse red blood cells.
Add 9 mL of BMIB to neutralize the Red Blood Cell Lysis Buffer.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C to pellet cells.
Discard supernatant and resuspend cells in 5 mL BMIB.
Pass the cell suspension through a pre-wetted 70-μm cell filter.
Centrifuge at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C to pellet cells.
Resuspend cells in complete DMEM/F12 containing 10% LCM medium pre-warmed to 37°C.
Prepare each 150 mm Petri dish with 25 mL DMEM/F12 containing 10% LCM medium.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension per dish and swirl to distribute cells evenly in the medium.
Incubate plates at 37°C in a 5% CO2 atmosphere.
Supplement each plate with fresh media on day 3 by adding 15 mL DMEM/F12 containing 10% LCM medium pre-warmed to 37°C.
Replace all media with 25 mL of fresh DMEM/F12 + 10% LCM on day 6.
Check cells under a microscope for spindle-like appearance, indicating macrophage development.
Aspirate the media from each plate on day 7.
Use a cell lifter to scrape cells from the Petri dishes or add 5 mL of Cellstripper per plate and incubate at 37°C for 10 minutes.
Collect the cell suspension and add 10 mL of DMEM/F12 medium to neutralize the Cellstripper.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 500 g for 5 minutes at 4°C to pellet cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in PBS or DMEM/F12 media and count the cell number using a hemocytometer.
Clean the work area with 70% ethanol.
Place a clean drape on a heating pad for surgery preparation.
Anesthetize adult mice (∼100 days old) with 2% isoflurane by nose cone.
Inject mice with analgesic, Meloxicam, at 2 mg/kg body weight subcutaneously.
Apply ophthalmic ointment to the eyes using sterile cotton-tipped applicators.
Shave both hindquarters of the mice carefully using shavers.
Clean the skin with 70% ethanol Prep Pads and betadine surgical scrub.
Cover the surgical field with a sterile drape.
Sterilize all instruments by autoclave or hot bead sterilization.
Wear a mask, gown, and sterile gloves for surgery.
Incise the skin just below the lateral aspect of the femur bone.
Open the fascial plane between the gluteus maximus and the anterior head of the biceps femoris with blunt scissors.
Reveal the sciatic nerve by gently freeing it from surrounding connective tissue without damaging or stretching the nerve.
Crush the sciatic nerve for 20 seconds using smooth forceps at three clicks, being careful not to stretch the nerve.
Place the crushed nerve carefully back in its original position.
Close the muscle fascia.
Close the skin incision using 9 mm reflex clips.
If 9 mm reflex clips restrict movement, use smaller reflex clips or 6-0 absorbable sutures instead.
Divide bone marrow cells from one animal into five 150 mm dishes for differentiation.
Wash the cells on day 7 with PBS.
Scrape in 5 mL of PBS using a cell lifter and collect in 15 mL tubes.
Spin the cells twice with PBS at 500 g for 5 min to eliminate carry-over media and FBS.
Pool the cells from all the tubes in one 15 mL tube and gently resuspend in 5 mL of PBS to make a homogeneous cell suspension.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Centrifuge the cell suspension again at 500 g for 5 min.
Resuspend the cells in PBS and gently mix the cells to produce a cell suspension such that each 100 μL contains 5 × 10^6 cells.
Heat tail regions of mice under the infrared lamp for 10–15 min.
Prepare syringes with cells for injection.
Keep syringes on ice.
Move a single mouse to the mouse retainer.
Pull the tail towards the investigator.
Hold the syringe in your dominant hand.
Position the syringe parallel to the tail.
Insert the needle with the bevel up into the lateral vein.
Slowly inject the cells.
Inject cells smoothly with minimal resistance.
If there is resistance to the injection or white blisters appear above the injection site, withdraw the needle and try a different proximal injection site.
Do not inject distal to the initial injection site if fluid has escaped via the first site.
Inject each animal 100 μL of BMDM suspension.
Remove the needle and press firmly with the thumb to prevent backflow of the injected solution and blood.
Apply gentle compression with a clean gauze/wipe or tissue until the bleeding has stopped.
